title: The global ocean circulation
summary: The global ocean conveyor belt is a constantly moving system of deep-ocean circulation driven by temperature and salinity. It starts in the Norwegian Sea, where water from the Gulf Stream loses heat, grows denser and sinks. Its past pattern changed with seaways: constriction of the Central American Seaway around 4.8 to 4 million years ago strengthened Atlantic overturning, with global climate effects, and constriction of the Indonesian Seaway followed between about 4 and 3 million years ago.
